q: What does the MQTT wildcard + match?
explain: + is single-level; # matches all remaining levels and must be last.

q: Which MQTT QoS gives exactly-once delivery?
explain: QoS 2 uses PUBLISH, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP so the receiver delivers the message once.

q: Why can MQTT QoS 1 deliver a message twice?
options: The PUBACK is lost, so the sender resends the PUBLISH
explain: At-least-once: a lost ack causes a resend (DUP flag), so handlers must be idempotent.

q: What is an MQTT retained message for?
options: Giving new subscribers the last known value immediately
explain: The broker keeps the last message of a topic and sends it to every new subscriber.

q: When is the MQTT Last Will message published?
explain: The broker publishes the will if the client dies without a clean DISCONNECT, which is how you detect 'offline'.

q: Best fit for millions of battery-powered sensors on mobile networks?
explain: MQTT has tiny headers, one long-lived connection, QoS levels and last will.
